The hMoI module for the XH component

Source: R/human-X-hMoI.R
hMoI.Rd

hMoI implements a model with two hybrid variables that track the mean Multiplicity of Infection (MoI): the first models the true MoI, and the second is the MoI for "younger" infections that are detected with higher frequency than older ones.

This model is derived under a restrictive set of assumptions, so it cannot be extended to model dynamic changes in population size or treatment with anti-malarial drugs.

Note

The force of infection is computed and stored by Exposure as FoI.

State Variables

m1 or \(m_1\)

mean MoI for all infections

m2 or \(m_2\)

mean MoI for apparent (detectable) infections

Demography

Demographic change is inconsistent with the model formulation. Human population density \((H)\) is a parameter, but it should be changed using change_XH_inits.

Dynamical Term

\(h\) or foi

The force of infection

In the hMoI module, there is no effect of pre-erythrocytic immunity, so a constant fraction of infectious bites causes an infection: the parameter \(b.\)

Parameters

r1 or \(r_1\)

clearance rate for all infections

r2 or \(r_2\)

clearance rate for apparent infections, \(r_2 > r_1\)

b

probability of infection per infectious bite

c1 or \(c_1\)

probability of transmitting from m1

c2 or \(c_2\)

probability of transmitting from m2

H

human or host population density

Infection Dynamics

$$ \begin{array}{rl} dm_1/dt &= h - r_1 m_1 \\ dm_2/dt &= h - r_2 m_2 \\ \end{array}$$

Prevalence

\(x_1\)

true prevalence: \(x_1 = 1-e^{-m_1}\)

\(x_2\)

apparent prevalence: \(x_2 = 1-e^{-m_2}\)

F_pr_obs.hMoI returns apparent prevalence \(x_2\). F_pfpr_by_lm, F_pfpr_by_rdt, and F_pfpr_by_pcr are compatibility aliases for F_pr_obs in this module.

Infectiousness

The model assumes that younger infections are more infectious, but that some transmission does occur from the older infections: $$c_2 x_2 + c_1 (x_1 - x_2)$$ so the infectious density is $$\left(c_2 x_2 + c_1 (x_1 - x_2)\right) H$$
